subject.title: fix(qqbot): queued and in-flight messages are lost when the gateway resumes after reconnect or restart

question: Should QQ Bot adopt at-least-once delivery across reconnects and restarts, accepting possible duplicate handling when a crash occurs after processing but before the throttled session save?
rationale: The code can prevent silent loss only by delaying the resumable cursor, but without a durable per-message acknowledgement or deduplication store that necessarily creates a bounded duplicate-delivery window; choosing that channel contract requires owner intent.

options.title: Accept bounded duplicates
options.body: Merge the settlement watermark after refreshed exact-head checks, treating occasional duplicate replay as preferable to silent message loss.

options.title: Require durable deduplication
options.body: Pause this PR and design persisted message identity or acknowledgement tracking before changing delivery semantics, accepting a substantially broader storage and migration change.

options.title: Retain current semantics
options.body: Close or decline the fix and keep receipt-time cursor commits, explicitly accepting queued and in-flight message loss during reconnect or restart.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded duplicates
recommendation.body: Merge the settlement watermark after refreshed exact-head checks, treating occasional duplicate replay as preferable to silent message loss.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the major QQ Bot gateway and queue architecture change and are the strongest available owner for the channel delivery-contract choice.
